newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran says more than 10,000 Kurds returned to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Iran says more than 10,000 Kurds returned to Iraq.

text.p: More than 10,500 Kurdish refugees who were among tens of thousands who fled fighting between Kurdish factions in northern Iraq in the past two months have returned home, an Iranian official said on Saturday.

The state-run Iranian news agency IRNA quoted Ahmad Hosseini, Iran's top official in charge of refugees, as saying that the refugees returned voluntarily and were provided with food and other necessities.

Hosseini said a total of 85,000 refugees had entered Iran and international efforts including financial aid would be required to shelter tens of thousands of others who were still in a buffer zone in the border region.
Hosseini said Iran had spent 70 billion rials ($23.3 million) on the refugees, of which 15 billion rials ($5 million) were provided by the United Nations.
A United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) official said last week the U.N. has given Iran $3 million. The cause for the apparent discrepancy between the two figures was not clear.
Iran has warned of bleak winter conditions and repeatedly complained of receiving little international funds to look after the refugees. In late August the Kurdistan
Democratic Party (KDP), backed by Iraqi troops, defeated the rival Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), triggering a mass exodus from northern Iraq.
More refugees crossed into neighbouring Iran when fighting erupted again in October and the PUK regained lost territory.
Iran is home to two million refugees, 1.4 million from Afghanistan and 600,000 from Iraq, making it the world's most important host country, according to the UNHCR.
($1 = 3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
